issue.title: Before function for persistent flags
issue.body:
This is with v3.0.0-beta1.01.
I came across this issue while porting our commands in [go-ethereum](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum) from v2 to v3.

In many of our tools, we use a `Before` hook on the root command to perform common actions such as setting up logging.
As an example, let's define a flag like this to set the loglevel:

```go
var logLevelFlag = &cli.IntFlag{
    Name: "loglevel",
    Value: 3,
}
```

The root command includes this flag and a `Before` hook to enable logging.

```go
var app = &cli.Command{
    Flags: []cli.Flag{
        logLevelFlag,
    },

    Commands: []*cli.Command{
        subCommand,
    },
    
    Before: func (ctx context.Context, cmd *cli.Command) (context.Context, error) {
        // here we would set the loglevel on the default logger
        fmt.Println("level:", cmd.Int(logLevelFlag.Name))
        return ctx, nil
    },
}

var subCommand = &cli.Command{
    Name: "sub",
}
```

This works as expected when invoking the root command (`app`) directly:

```shell
$ ./app --loglevel=5
level: 5
```

It also works for subcommands when putting the flag before the command:

```shell
$ ./app --loglevel=5 sub
level: 5
```

But it doesn't work when the flag is at the end:

```shell
$ ./app sub --loglevel=5
level: 3  # should be 5
```

It's unexpected behavior for me, because in v3, flags are supposed to be persistent by default, i.e. they should be applicable in any context. I think

comments.author: fjl
comments.body:
I think it's an inconsistent behavior, anyway. It's weird because the flag is defined at the root command level, but its value is not available for root command.

I have posted PR #2028 to show a possible resolution. Let me know what you think.

comments.author: fjl
comments.body: Let me just iterate again why the current behavior is weird: the purpose of the cli library is creating a command structure. In the end, running the CLI app will resolve a single command, and run its action function. The goal of flag parsing, hooks, etc.  is setting up things for this resolved action. comments.body: The term 'persistent flag', in the context of this project, means a flag that is defined in a parent command, but can be given to a subcommand. The opposite is 'local flag'. See https://github.com/urfave/cli/issues/1820
